entries.test: Published access correspondence, acknowledgments, and experiment records could establish whether third parties supplied the access that enabled Marcus and Davis's analyses.
entries.note: The central claim explains what enabled their analyses; the corporate-science aside adds evaluative language.

entries.test: Public evaluations of models available by June 7, 2022, against the Technology Review article's identified reasoning and reliability problems would establish whether those general failures persisted despite corrected examples.
entries.note: The referenced article and enumerated problem categories anchor the claim. 'So far as I can tell' qualifies his assessment without making it a possibility claim.
The passage supplies no shared criterion for possessing a cognitive model of the world. Readers could agree on model behavior while disagreeing about whether it demonstrates such a model.

entries.test: Public controlled scaling experiments and ablations varying training-data size, model size, and training methods would establish whether larger datasets primarily explain the newer models' improvements.
entries.note: Identifying the primary cause is difficult but empirically testable.
The architecture condition carries over from the preceding paragraph. The central prediction is firm, but 'a genuine causal model of the world' lacks a shared evidentiary criterion.

entries.test: Published outputs and comparative scoring across the complete Technology Review question set would show whether InstructGPT produced fewer nonsensical answers, corrected some earlier failures, and regressed on some earlier successes.
entries.note: Marcus asserts Davis's finding in his own voice. The concrete pattern of improvements and regressions makes the comparison testable despite its subjective expectation language.
